key_insight: A reinforcement learning agent trained entirely in simulation autonomously positions a PIV camera to locate and resolve hydrofoil wakes after zero-shot transfer to a real water tunnel.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive camera placement can improve flow-measurement resolution and accuracy while reducing acquisition time and image requirements.
method: Formulate camera placement as sequential control of a camera-equipped 6-DoF manipulator.
Use PIV-estimated velocity fields and uncertainty as the agent’s scene observations.
Train in a photorealistic water-tunnel simulation using CFD wakes spanning hydrofoil profiles, positions and angles of attack.
evidence_signal: Real-water-tunnel tests with randomly placed hydrofoils showed reliable wake framing, higher resolution and lower flow-statistics error than a fixed view, using roughly half the time of a full scan and far fewer image pairs.
watch_item: Transfer beyond the tested water-tunnel setup remains unestablished in the abstract and may depend on simulation fidelity and PIV uncertainty estimation.
paper_title: Autonomous Particle Image Velocimetry Using Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning
